_comment: Executable claims for OPEN-DECISIONS.md, one JSON object per line. `status` is the state of THIS CLAIM, not of the whole OD entry — an entry can be partly resolved (OD-56's Python half is fixed while its Node transitives are not, so its aiohttp/cryptography claim is `resolved` while OD-56 itself stays open). resolved = the claim MUST hold; if it stops holding, the fix regressed. open = the claim must NOT hold yet; if it starts holding, strike that part of the entry off. See scripts/check_decision_claims.sh and CLAUDE.md §5b.

claim: analytics.controller.ts is guarded (no longer an unauthenticated paid-LLM surface)
verify: grep -q '@UseGuards' apps/api-gateway/src/analytics/analytics.controller.ts

claim: jwt-secret.ts throws rather than falling back to a published string
verify: grep -q 'throw new Error' apps/api-gateway/src/auth/jwt-secret.ts

claim: SimposController is guarded AND SimposModule stays gated out of production
verify: grep -q 'UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)' apps/api-gateway/src/simpos/simpos.controller.ts && grep -q 'NODE_ENV !== "production" ? \[SimposModule\]' apps/api-gateway/src/app.module.ts

claim: no bare fetch() of a user-supplied URL remains in vendor-page-extractor — both sites go through safeFetch
verify: test "$(grep -c 'await fetch(' apps/api-gateway/src/vendor-intel/vendor-page-extractor.service.ts)" = 0 && test "$(grep -c 'safeFetch(' apps/api-gateway/src/vendor-intel/vendor-page-extractor.service.ts)" = 2

claim: splitPdfIfLarge caps pages, so chunk count cannot track an uploaded PDF's page count
verify: grep -q 'MAX_PAGES' apps/api-gateway/src/menus/parsers/scan-parser.service.ts && grep -q 'effectivePages' apps/api-gateway/src/menus/parsers/scan-parser.service.ts

claim: the four pos_* tables carry foreign keys (was 3, now 13)
verify: test "$(grep -c 'foreign key' supabase/migrations/20260825140000_pos_referential_integrity.sql)" -ge 10

claim: aiohttp and cryptography are pinned at or above their patched versions (the Python half of OD-56; the Node transitives are separate and still open)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('services/agent-orchestrator/requirements.txt').read(); a=re.search(r'^aiohttp==(\\S+)',s,re.M).group(1); c=re.search(r'^cryptography==(\\S+)',s,re.M).group(1); v=lambda x:[int(n) for n in x.split('.')]; sys.exit(0 if v(a)>=[3,14,3] and v(c)>=[50,0,0] else 1)"

claim: calendar_agent's regex fallback is NOT fed the prompt template (fixed in #57; the separate question of provider_important_dates not existing in production is OD-68)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('services/agent-orchestrator/agents/calendar_agent.py').read(); sys.exit(1 if re.search(r'_regex_date_extraction\\(\\s*prompt\\s*\\)', s) else 0)"

claim: no file in apps/web/src imports the browser anon-key Supabase client any more (OD-45 removed useReportQueries; useSommelierQueries is the last one). Holds when the sommelier surface is routed through the gateway, or when the hook is deleted
verify: test "$(grep -rl 'lib/supabase' apps/web/src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' | grep -v 'src/lib/supabase.ts' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 0

claim: a migration revokes anon's DML on the procurement document tables, so the invoice store is not readable/writable with the public anon key
verify: python3 -c "import glob,re,sys; pat=re.compile(r'revoke\s+all[^;]*\bprocurement_documents\b[^;]*\bfrom\b[^;]*\banon\b',re.I|re.S); sys.exit(0 if [f for f in glob.glob('supabase/migrations/*.sql') if pat.search(open(f,errors='ignore').read())] else 1)"

claim: increment_trust_counter(uuid) and seed_sim_restaurant(jsonb) are closed to anon/authenticated by 20260917010400: it revokes EXECUTE from public, anon and authenticated (OD-72 revoked only the last two, and both inherit PUBLIC's built-in grant), re-grants service_role, and asserts has_function_privilege is false for anon/authenticated and true for service_role before it reports success. The CLASS is held by scripts/check_definer_functions_closed.py, the end-state check: schema-parity.yml runs it as the step right after `supabase db reset --no-seed` -- first a canary with the allowlist emptied, which must report supabase_functions.http_request() (the local stack's platform webhook, SECURITY DEFINER and granted to anon/authenticated by the pinned CLI), then the real run, whose `DEFINER-CHECK OK -- <k> in public` line is asserted with k >= 7 (MIN_PUBLIC_SECDEF = 7) -- and a --self-test step that asserts at least 61 cases run [CORRECTED 2026-09-19, PR #391 audit, Notes to close: stale prose, never updated as the brackets below raised this floor -- it now asserts at least 576 cases run, the value in force per this row's own verify]. It fails when any SECURITY DEFINER function outside the system schemas and outside extensions answers to PUBLIC, anon or authenticated (by the built-in default, a grant, ownership or role membership) unless CLIENT_CALLABLE excuses it with an ADR. This row pins those two steps, their position and their floors statically, and runs the self-test. Arm (c) of scripts/check_new_tables_are_locked_down.py is a fast pre-check for common spellings, not the authority; this row also pins its ci.yml steps and its report (arm-(c) OK tally, self-test at least 89 cases) [CORRECTED 2026-09-19, PR #391 audit, Notes to close: stale prose -- arm (c)'s self-test floor is now 95, the value in force per this row's own verify]. ~~The CLASS is held by arm (c) of scripts/check_new_tables_are_locked_down.py, a CI step with its own --self-test step [...]: [...] none may be client-executable when the corpus finishes [...]~~ [CORRECTED 2026-09-18, round 5, source: PR #391 verifier round 4: a lexical arm cannot hold the class. Four review rounds each found spellings that re-open a definer while arm (c) exits 0 (a single-quoted DO body, `to group anon`, a grant to a role anon is a member of, a revoke under `if false` or undone by a savepoint, dynamic EXECUTE shapes, rename-then-grant, overloads). Replayed as migrations on a full-corpus build, the end-state check exits 1 on every one that leaks; see ADR 0159. Arm (c)'s three rules stand as a pre-check: same-file revoke, the end state as its replay of the text models it, and the per-schema no-op refused.] [Added 2026-09-18, round 4, source: PR #391 verifier round 3: arm (c) reads static migration text. Dynamic SQL (a variable, `||`, concat(), a later format() argument, `execute (...)`) is out of its reach except the EXECUTEd-literal shapes its --self-test names; see ADR 0159 Decision, residuals.] [CORRECTED 2026-09-18, source: PR #391 audit: the 2026-09-17 row certified that no-op as the class fix by grepping for its text. See ADR 0159.] This row pins the repo, not production: read 2026-09-18, production has not applied 20260917010400 and increment_trust_counter is still =X/postgres there. [Added 2026-09-18, source: PR #391 verifier: the verify trusted only the guard's exit codes, so the guard gutted to exit 0 (at its entry point, at the top of main(), or at the top of run_self_test()) left it green. It now asserts what the guard prints: the arm-(c) OK line with at least 7 SECURITY DEFINER creates on the real tree, and SELF-TEST OK with at least 89 cases run; the floor was 32 until the round-2 verifier's bypass shapes added ten self-test cases, and 42 until round 4 pinned every arm-(c) rule (47 more cases).] [2026-09-18, round 6, source: PR #391 verifier round 5: the allowlist matched on signature alone, so dropping supabase_functions.http_request() and recreating it as a callable definer granted to anon passed (A1c); a role granted to authenticator was not judged (A8); and this row stayed green under `if: false` on the self-test step (M1) and a neutered canary condition (M2). The end-state check now judges PUBLIC plus every role authenticator is a member of (service_role excepted, with its reason), and excuses an allowlisted function only while its identity matches the pin (owner, language, return type, returns-set, kind, proconfig, md5(prosrc) cb8a5741f829fe414ecd51c25be75c9a, measured from the v2.116.0 template); arm (c) refuses any migration naming supabase_functions (exit 2). This row now pins the canary's three lines verbatim and adjacent, the self-test step's `if:` exactly, the pinned owner and md5 in the script, arm (c)'s narrowed OK line, and floors of 105 (end-state self-test) and 95 (arm (c) self-test).] [2026-09-19, round 7, source: the founder's call on round 6's named residuals -- "do what the optimal scenario would do, no we can do this later or second plan": the end-state check now also fails on a SECURITY DEFINER function PostgreSQL runs for a judged role with no EXECUTE check against it (ADR 0159, REACH THROUGH ANOTHER OBJECT): a trigger on any write a judged role can make land on its table (directly, through a column privilege, an auto-updatable view, a rule, a partition or inheritance child, or a foreign-key CASCADE/SET NULL/SET DEFAULT action as the table's owner), everything else a cascaded table's objects call, index and statistics expressions under autoanalyze or MAINTAIN, a materialized view's query under REFRESH, the eight support functions of an aggregate a judged role may EXECUTE, a function taking or returning a type a judged role owns, and -- as PUBLIC -- every function the catalog wires into operator families, estimators, planner support, types, ranges, casts, event triggers, text search, languages, foreign-data wrappers, access methods, conversions, transforms and TABLESAMPLE. PR #391 verifier rows A3 and A9 (and the round-6 verifier's N1) now exit 1. This row now greps the trigger arm, the aggregate arm and the classifier's reach-through merge in the script, and asserts a self-test floor of 342 (was 105) in the step and in its own run.] [2026-09-19, round-7 repair, source: the round-7 verifier (NOT READY: no adversarial pass, no number re-run, and an open question that the reach query followed only an object's direct pg_depend rows to pg_proc). Measured on PGlite: 23 of 44 adversarial plants ran a closed definer as an object's owner for anon while the round-7 check exited 0 -- an operator, a domain cast, a SQL-standard body, a policy's subquery or a whole-row reference in an owner-context object, a row an UPDATE moves between partitions, a view over a view with INSTEAD OF triggers, PL/pgSQL or a builtin that runs SQL text in owner context, and functions, types or relations a judged role owns. The end-state check now walks what every owner-context object names and exits 1 on a definer it reaches, 2 (BLIND) on owner-context code the catalog does not describe; all 44 plants give the wanted exit and every control exits 0 (ADR 0159, round-7 repair). Each query is now pinned by the md5 of its exact text (QUERIES_MD5), since the repair's mutation table showed a clause pin cannot see a falsifier added beside it. This row now also greps the walk's dependency edge, the opaque-body BLIND rule, the walk's rows in the verdict, the exit-2 wiring of BLIND, the md5 comparison and REACH_SQL's pinned md5 (7b2f0774372a11aeaff6cb518075f64b, the text the repair's replay measured), and asserts a self-test floor of 491 (was 342) in the step and in its own run.] [2026-09-19, round-7 repair 2, source: the round-7 verifier's re-run (NOT READY: no adversarial pass, no number re-measured, and an open question that owner-context paths reach a function through catalog objects the walk does not follow). A second adversarial pass on PGlite (27 plants, 22 controls) found six more paths the first repair's check passed with exit 0 while a closed definer ran for anon: ANALYZE of a column with no index runs its type's statistics code as the owner (a range's subtype_diff: C1); a foreign key's CHECK, not only its actions, runs as the other table's owner, casts included (C2, C2n); the planner swaps an operator for its negator (C3, C3m, C3i); builtins take a type or a table by bare OID (domain_in, record_in, array_in: C4, C4r, C4a; satisfies_hash_partition: C5); a partition's constraint runs its parent's partition key (C7); and, in plain client context, a selectivity estimator runs the operator's own function (or its negator's or commutator's) on column statistics while planning, with no EXECUTE check (C10: anon's EXPLAIN ran the closed definer six times). The check now seeds column statistics and foreign-key checks, follows negators and commutators, adds the five type-by-OID builtins and satisfies_hash_partition to the BLIND list, judges the estimator path as PUBLIC, and walks once per seed object (the storage-api proxy: 97.5 s to 3.0 s on PGlite). All 27 plants give the wanted exit and every control exits 0. This row now also greps the estimator arm, the column-statistics seed, the foreign-key-check seed and the per-seed-object walk, pins REACH_SQL's new md5 (6d61c09d09ad23185b7c69545bbb15eb) and asserts a self-test floor of 576 (was 491) in the step and in its own run.]

claim: Outbound MIME headers are RFC 2047 encoded and cannot be injected (ADR 0172, Proposed 2026-09-19). The two hand-built Gmail messages in apps/api-gateway write every header through communications/mime-headers.ts: GmailService.createMimeMessage's From (the house's own name per ADR 0149, defaulting to Mudavym, handed to the encoder raw so quotes are escaped rather than deleted), To, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References and Subject, and sendThroughGrant's (letters/house-letters.service.ts) From, To and Subject. Subject and display names become =?UTF-8?B?...?= words split on whole characters, every line at most 76 characters, with CR/LF and other control characters collapsed to one space. Addresses are trimmed, then refused on an interior control character. A named entry (ending in <addr>) must hold exactly one mailbox: a quoted name that is not one quoted-string ("A" <a@x>, "B" <b@x>) or an unquoted name containing <, >, @ or , (A <a@x>, B <b@x>; a@x, B <b@x>) is refused, never collapsed; a bare a@x, b@y list is written as before. Our own Message-ID is refused on a control character. A refusal returns success:false with refusedBeforeSend and Gmail is never called; sendProviderEmail throws SendRefusedBeforeSendError and isDefiniteSendRefusal recognises it by instanceof, never by text (the text embeds the vendor's address), so the draft is released and the error names the header, not GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN. The vendor's In-Reply-To/References are REBUILT from their <msg-id> tokens (threadingHeader; an id too long for a 998-character line is dropped), never refused: RFC 5322 folding (CRLF+TAB) in stored vendor values used to make every reply on that thread fail. Body parts are Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64. Static verify, exactly: (1) a sweep that no non-spec .ts under apps/api-gateway/src has a LINE-LEADING header template literal (`Subject: ${ ... at the start of a line) — it does not catch a template literal mid-line (e.g. a ternary), and it cannot be widened to any position because gmail.service.ts sendEmail logs `Subject: ${options.subject}`; (2) grep -Fq pins on every one of the 12 header calls listed above, which is what catches a mid-line raw header; (3) the two base64 CTE lines, the guards in mime-headers.ts (collapse, refuse, code-point split, fold budget, threading token regex and length bound, trim-before-refuse, the two multi-mailbox refusals), the typed procurement refusal and its instanceof classification (with no 'Refusing to write' text match left in procurement.service.ts), and five spec titles. Fails on origin/main 08c04100e at the sweep. Each of the 12 header pins mutation-proven red on this branch. Not covered: the nodemailer SMTP fallback (encodes and folds CRLF itself, measured on nodemailer 8.0.1) and the Python senders (email.mime; see v3.0-TECH-DEBT 'Outbound MIME: what ADR 0172 does not cover').

claim: No unanchored directory pattern in .vercelignore shadows a tracked file under apps/ or packages/ — counting `X`, `X/`, `**/X` and any case variant of them, because the Vercel uploader's ignore engine treats all four the same and matches at any depth. A bare `logs` did exactly that twice, silently: the uploader prunes the directory before it ever looks inside, so the only symptom was a build error naming a module that is plainly present in git. Hand-fixed 2026-09-12, hand-fixed again in PR #428; this row is the guard that stops a third time. Against origin/main's .vercelignore it exits 1 and names 13 files, which is what makes it a test and not a restatement. Hardened in round 4 of #428's own audit: the first draft skipped any pattern containing `*`, and .vercelignore already carries four `**/`-prefixed entries as its house style, so an editor writing `**/logs` would have reintroduced the bug with CI green.

This browser keeps only a MIRROR of what the account said, so every `localStorage` reach in `groundChoice.ts` must go through `groundMirrorKey(userId)` -- a single device-wide key (what rounds 1-5 shipped) is what would let one person on a shared terminal inherit another's ground, and is the specific regression this half exists to prevent. `index.html`'s pre-paint script, which runs before React and so cannot call any of the above, must build the same per-person key from the `sub` claim of the session's own access token.
